Publish from Houdini#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — built and unit-tested, needs a real Houdini install.** The plug-in's code ran against a fake hou: the glTF / FBX ROP choice and parameters, cleanup of the temporary ROP, the world-space bounding box, scene-unit scaling, the interruptable operation (Esc = cancel), batch mode, settings, the shelf file and the package file. A GLB it exported was published to a real local Verse server and finished (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). Nothing has been run inside Houdini yet.

A Verse shelf with Publish to Verse, Publish Selection and Verse Settings. The geometry in /obj is written to GLB by a temporary ROP glTF Output, uploaded with progress, and the share link is copied and opened — a link that opens on any phone.

You need: Houdini 19.5 or newer (Python 3). Windows, macOS or Linux.

1. Install#

Download VersePublish-Houdini-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it:

Code
sh integrations/aec/houdini/make_package.sh   # -> integrations/aec/houdini/dist/VersePublish-Houdini-4.0.0-beta.1.zip

Unzip somewhere stable. In Houdini's Windows ▸ Python Shell:

Code
exec(open(r"C:/Tools/VersePublish-Houdini/install_houdini.py").read())

It writes packages/VersePublish.json in your Houdini preferences folder, pointing at the unzipped VersePublish folder. Restart Houdini and add the shelf with the shelf set's + ▸ Shelves ▸ Verse.

2. Server and key#

Verse Settings — server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token, bake lighting and scene unit. Save for every Verse plug-in shares server, key and token with the other tools.

Nothing is compiled in. Settings live in the per-user settings.json every Verse plug-in shares, houdini section (%APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\ on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Ctruh/VersePublish/ on macOS, ~/.config/ctruh/verse-publish/ on Linux). VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY, VERSE_TOKEN override it — handy on a farm.

3. Publish#

  1. Publish to Verse (all geometry OBJ nodes in /obj) or select OBJ nodes and Publish Selection.
  2. Houdini's interrupt dialog shows uploading % → building stages. Esc or its stop button cancels and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. Published! — the link is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: Published! with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); the geometry opens at its real size in metres.

Batch / farm: hython -c "import verse_publish_houdini as v; v.publish_hip('shot.hip')" publishes /obj of a hip file and prints the link (no dialogs).

What gets exported#

  • GLB through a temporary ROP glTF Output (/out, removed afterwards).
  • FBX through a ROP FBX Output with embedded media if the glTF ROP is not available; the server converts it. Without the glTF ROP, Publish Selection takes one OBJ node at a time.
  • Units. Houdini's convention, 1 unit = 1 metre, is glTF's, so nothing changes by default. A hip built in centimetres (or mm / in / ft) sets Scene unit; the GLB is then measured against the scene and wrapped in one metre-scale root node if needed.
  • Packed primitives, instances and USD/Solaris stages: export what the glTF ROP supports; for a LOP network, publish its USD from the IFC and USD guide instead.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in the Verse Settings shelf tool (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in the Verse Settings shelf tool.
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
No Verse shelf to addThe Houdini package from install_houdini.py was not loaded.Run install_houdini.py again in the Python Shell and restart Houdini.
"Houdini could not export the scene as glTF or FBX. …"No glTF / FBX ROP could render the scene.Check a ROP glTF Output renders by hand, then publish again.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.

What has been tested#

ROP choice and parameters, temporary ROP removed, world bounding box, scene unit, multi-selection FBX refusal, empty /obj / selection sentences, interrupt = cancel, batch mode, settings, shelf XML, package JSON — against a fake houtested
A GLB exported through the plug-in published to a real local server, scene donetested
The glTF and FBX ROPs' parameter names in your build, the interrupt dialog during an upload, package + shelf loading inside Houdinineeds a real install
